coverage: Selected implemented rules and high-risk distinctions, not a complete normative specification.

nodes.title: Blocks and bindings
nodes.semantics: A block returns its final expression. let bindings are immutable. Function boundaries have explicit types.
pitfalls: No assignment or return statement
Do not shadow visible names

nodes.title: Nominal records
nodes.semantics: A record groups named typed fields. Construction supplies every field. Nominal identity, not field similarity, determines the type.
pitfalls: Records are immutable
Empty and partial records are not admitted

nodes.title: Record updates
nodes.semantics: Type { ...base, field: value } constructs a new value. Evaluate the same-nominal base once, then overrides once in written order.
pitfalls: Three dots, one base first
Empty values replace fields; they are not skipped

nodes.title: Variants
nodes.semantics: A nominal variant chooses one named case, optionally carrying a typed payload. Expected types can identify a case owner.
pitfalls: A case is not a record field
Bare payload-free cases need an identifying expected type

nodes.title: Exhaustive match
nodes.semantics: match selects the case of a variant and binds its payload. Every case occurs exactly once and all arm results have the same type.
pitfalls: All arms are checked, even unreachable arms

nodes.title: Result propagation
nodes.semantics: Prefix try unwraps Ok(T) or returns Err(E) from the enclosing function. Operand and output must each have exactly the payload cases Ok and Err with matching error types.
pitfalls: No implicit resource cleanup
try(value) remains a function call
Runtime faults are not caught; postconditions still run

nodes.title: Persistent lists
nodes.semantics: List<T> is immutable. prepend(value,list) returns a new first element followed by the old list. head/tail require a nonempty list.
pitfalls: Prepending reverses traversal order
No built-in append or indexing operation

nodes.title: Counted fold
nodes.semantics: fold(i in n,state:T=initial) returns successive typed states for indices 0 through n-1. Zero iterations return initial.
pitfalls: A record carries multiple state fields
Count must be nonnegative; fuel still applies

nodes.title: State-driven while
nodes.semantics: while(state:T=initial; condition) repeatedly evaluates a condition and replaces the state with the body value. The result is the last state.
pitfalls: No break or continue statement; carry stop state
Finite fuel can stop a nonterminating loop

nodes.title: Bytes and byte ranges
nodes.semantics: Bytes stores raw immutable octets. Bytes::at returns an integer 0..255. Bytes::slice(data,start,count) uses a byte count.
pitfalls: The third slice argument is not an end offset
Empty Bytes is a value; indexing it faults

nodes.title: UTF-8 text
nodes.semantics: Text stores valid UTF-8. Text::length/at/slice index Unicode scalar values. Text::bytes gives the UTF-8 Bytes view.
pitfalls: Scalar positions are not byte offsets or grapheme positions
There is no implicit Text/Bytes conversion

nodes.title: Generic inference
nodes.semantics: Generic functions, records and variants are checked parametrically. Local argument and expected constructor contexts can infer type arguments when they determine every parameter consistently.
pitfalls: Explicit specialization remains available
No global case-name search or whole-program inference
Function boundaries still need types

nodes.title: Named callbacks
nodes.semantics: Fn(A) actions { action.id } -> B describes a named function value. Named references capture no environment. Signature parameters, result and action set match exactly.
pitfalls: Omitted action clause means pure
Pass context as an argument
No action widening or captured closures

nodes.title: Declared actions
nodes.semantics: A function declares an upper bound on its actions. Every direct and callback invocation must fit that bound, including unreachable code.
pitfalls: A declaration does not grant resource authority
Actionful callbacks are checked by exact declared sets

nodes.title: Typed permissions
nodes.semantics: Native and SQL libraries expose typed permission collections for capability restriction. Derived capabilities can remove rights. Launch grants bound root authority.
pitfalls: Permissions are authority, actions are behavior
Typed collections wrap a closed provider catalog; arbitrary FFI is absent

nodes.title: Execution limits
nodes.semantics: Fuel, heap, depth and native operation/byte limits bound invocations. Native resource operations also obey deadlines and explicit launch grants.
pitfalls: Limits do not prove termination or functional correctness
Quota exhaustion and typed IO errors have distinct behavior

nodes.title: Stable identities
nodes.semantics: Adjacent .lobo.ids.json files bind declaration/import names to persistent IDs. Explicit init/sync/rename authoring commands manage bindings. Checks never allocate IDs.
pitfalls: Preserve ID values when renaming; retarget keys
Do not derive established identities from names or bodies

nodes.title: Closed imports
nodes.semantics: use group { name }; binds selected declarations by stable identity. Supply every source explicitly. The loader does not discover dependency files by path.
pitfalls: A source spelling is not the persistent identity
Compilation requires the complete explicit source bundle

nodes.title: JSON literals
nodes.semantics: JSON literal syntax uses the supplied JSON library builders by stable ID. Json and directly called helpers stay explicit. The compiler records generated builder imports.
pitfalls: Supply the JSON source dependency
Literal syntax does not imply a database or network grant

nodes.title: Native compilation
nodes.semantics: compile/run use machine code by default through the C backend. Direct LLVM is optional. eval is the reference evaluator for correctness comparisons.
pitfalls: No projection step is needed
The proposed workspace daemon and self-hosting are not implemented

source_refs.anchor: The language is experimental; the wider workspace, WASM backend, and self-hosting are future work.

nodes.title: Study input encoding
nodes.semantics: Input JSON encodings belong to each experiment protocol and its trusted adapters. A hexadecimal JSON string can encode Bytes; this is not a Lobo expression.
pitfalls: Do not infer a wire schema from source types alone
Schema changes need identical input documentation across comparison languages
